title: Database branching for AI agents
body: A branch is a copy-on-write fork of a database. Agents can run destructive SQL on a branch and throw it away afterwards, so production is never touched.

title: Vacuum and table bloat
body: Updates and deletes leave dead tuples behind. Autovacuum reclaims the space and keeps the visibility map current so index-only scans stay fast.

title: Choosing the right index
body: B-tree handles equality and range queries, GIN handles arrays, jsonb and full-text search, and BRIN suits huge append-only tables ordered by time.

title: Vector search with HNSW
body: The pgvector HNSW index gives approximate nearest-neighbour search over embeddings. Tune ef_search to trade recall for latency.

title: Full-text search basics
body: A tsvector stores normalized lexemes and a tsquery describes what to match. websearch_to_tsquery accepts quotes, OR and a leading minus like a search engine.

title: Fuzzy matching with trigrams
body: The pg_trgm extension splits text into three-character sequences. Similarity and word_similarity find matches even when the user makes a typo.

title: The write-ahead log
body: Every change is written to the write-ahead log before the data files. After a crash, Postgres replays the log to reach a consistent state.

title: Streaming replication
body: A standby server receives the write-ahead log from the primary over the network and replays it, staying a few milliseconds behind.

title: Connection pooling
body: Postgres forks a process per connection. A pooler such as PgBouncer in transaction mode lets thousands of clients share a few server connections.

title: LISTEN and NOTIFY
body: NOTIFY sends a message to every session listening on a channel when the transaction commits. It needs a session-level connection, not a transaction-mode pooler.

title: Job queues with SKIP LOCKED
body: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lets many workers claim different rows from the same table without blocking each other.

title: Working with jsonb
body: jsonb stores parsed JSON. The containment operator @> and a GIN index make lookups inside documents fast.

title: Table partitioning
body: Declarative partitioning splits a large table by range, list or hash. Old partitions can be detached and dropped instantly instead of deleted row by row.

title: Reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE
body: EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the query and reports the real time and row counts of each plan node. Compare estimated and actual rows to spot bad statistics.

title: Row level security
body: Policies attached to a table filter which rows each role can see or modify, enforcing tenant isolation inside the database.

title: Sequences and identity columns
body: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY is the standard way to create auto-incrementing keys. Sequence values are never rolled back, so gaps are normal.

title: Common table expressions
body: WITH queries name intermediate results. A recursive CTE walks trees and graphs such as org charts or category hierarchies.

title: Materialized views
body: A materialized view stores the result of a query. REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY updates it without blocking readers when it has a unique index.

title: Point-in-time recovery
body: With a base backup and archived write-ahead log you can restore a database to any moment, for example just before an accidental DROP TABLE.

title: Extensions
body: Extensions such as pgvector, pg_trgm and pg_stat_statements add types, operators and views. CREATE EXTENSION installs one into the current database.
